walkthroughs.body_html:
Aspects of French-speaking Society: Current Issues — a core area of A-Level French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Aspects of French-speaking Society: Current Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Aspects of French-speaking Society: Current Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which French verb form correctly says 'I would have helped' (j'... aidé)?
options: aurai
aurais
avait
étais

mcqs.q: Which conjunction always triggers the subjunctive?
options: parce que
car
bien que
puisque

mcqs.q: Which verbs take 'être' as their auxiliary in the passé composé?
options: Just movement verbs - never reflexives.
All verbs take avoir.
Movement/state-change verbs (DR & MRS VAN DER TRAMP) and all reflexive verbs.
Le is masculine, lui is feminine.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I'm going to my friend's house' in French?
options: Je vais chez mon ami.
Je vais à la maison de mon ami.
All verbs take avoir.
Je vais à mon ami.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'le' and 'lui' as pronouns?
options: Je vais à mon ami.
They are interchangeable.
Le is masculine, lui is feminine.
Le replaces a direct object (him/it); lui replaces an indirect object (to him/her).
